It allocates entirely new arrays (`next_values` and `next_costs`) at each level of the tree, which can be optimized by updating the existing arrays in-place from left to right, saving memory and time.

The use of `input().strip()` to read the second line is vulnerable to breaking if there happen to be trailing spaces on the first line or empty lines before the string; using `sys.stdin.read().split()` is more robust against any whitespace irregularities.
